name: Timna
title: Concubine of Esau's grandson
summary: Timna was a concubine to Eliphaz, who was the son of Esau. She was the mother of Amalek, the ancestor of the Amalekites, a people who later became one of Israel's most persistent enemies. Timna is also mentioned as a sister of the Horite chief Lotan.

keyEvents.title: Timna as Eliphaz's concubine
keyEvents.description: Timna is mentioned as a concubine to Eliphaz, the son of Esau. Through this connection, she became linked to Esau's lineage.

keyEvents.title: Mother of Amalek
keyEvents.description: Timna bore Amalek to Eliphaz. Amalek became the ancestor of the Amalekites, a people who later became one of Israel's bitterest enemies.

keyEvents.title: Sister of Lotan
keyEvents.description: Timna is identified as the sister of Lotan, one of the Horite chiefs in the land of Seir. This shows her connection to the Horites.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned among Esau's descendants
keyEvents.description: In Chronicles, Timna's place in the genealogy is repeated as Eliphaz's concubine and mother of Amalek, emphasizing her role in tribal history.

keyEvents.title: The Horite Chiefs in Seir
keyEvents.description: Timna's brother Lotan is mentioned among the Horite chiefs who lived in the land of Seir before Esau's descendants took over the area.
